name: Job
charge: Perfect and upright, fearing God and eschewing evil; sinning not with his lips in all his loss
summary: Job of Uz feared God and eschewed evil. Under a trial limited by God's command, he lost his substance, his children, and then his health, yet held fast his integrity. When God answered, Job humbled himself and repented of words beyond his understanding. He prayed for his accusing friends, and the Lord restored him.
offense: The commendation is given by God before the trial and repeated after it began: hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God and escheweth evil (Job 1:8), and still he holdeth fast his integrity, although thou movedst me against him to destroy him without cause (Job 2:3). The obedience is not endurance only. He acted as a priest for his own household: when the days of their feasting were gone about, and every one had kept his day, Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all, for Job said, it may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts; thus did Job continually (Job 1:5). His defence recalls practical righteousness: when he went out to the gate through the city, the young men saw him and hid themselves, the aged arose and stood, the princes refrained talking, and the nobles held their peace (Job 29:7-10). He delivered the poor that cried and the fatherless, was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame, searched out a cause he did not know before judging it, and broke the jaws of the wicked and plucked the spoil out of his teeth (Job 29:12-17). He also made a covenant with his eyes (Job 31:1). His righteousness included investigation, not merely sympathy: he sought the facts and rescued the oppressed from the wicked. That stands against his friends' readiness to explain his suffering by accusing him without establishing their charge. Satan's charge was that the obedience  was bought: doth Job fear God for nought, hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side (Job 1:9-10). The trial has limits set by God. Satan asked leave and was given it in limits both times: all that he hath is in thy power, only upon himself put not forth thine hand (Job 1:12), and then, behold, he is in thine hand, but save his life (Job 2:6). And when the property, the servants and all ten children were taken in a single day, he worshipped and said, the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away, blessed be the name of the Lord; in all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly (Job 1:20-22). After his body was afflicted, his wife urged him to abandon his integrity: dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die (Job 2:9), and he answered her, thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh; what, shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips (Job 2:10).
judgment: The Lord turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before. So the Lord blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, seven sons and three daughters, and in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job; and he saw his sons' sons, even four generations. James: ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord; that the Lord is very pitiful, and of tender mercy.

entries.commentary: This first verse tells you who Job is, what land he lived in, and his character. Just because he lived in the land of Uz does not mean he was of that nation, because he was a son of God. It is the same thing today: we live in America but we are not Caucasians. There are brothers that live in Europe and they are not Caucasians either, but they are the sons of God.

Job had seven sons and three daughters, and his substance was seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen and five hundred she asses, so that this man was the greatest of all the men of the east. His sons went and feasted in their houses, every one his day. When it says "every man his day," they were talking about their birthdays. Whenever somebody's birthday came around they would say, "this is my day, this is my day." Now people have gotten to the point where it is, "this is my month, my birthday month, so I am celebrating the whole month." Same thing with this. Job sanctified them and rose up early to offer burnt offerings according to the number of them all, for Job said it may be that his sons had sinned and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually. -

When it says "the sons of God," this is talking about the line, the lineage of Adam. Before we were called Israelites we were called the sons of God, and even still today we are called the sons of the living God. So this is talking about the same thing; it is not just talking about angels alone. -

This is Satan talking to the Lord. The Lord says, have you considered My servant Job, have you ever tried Job, you walking up and down the earth, have you tried My servant, because he is an upright man. It is the same thing with us today. Every time we do more good works, the harder Satan comes at you. When you fast, the trials get worse, because you are showing God that you are upright through your fasting, striving to be that righteous vessel He wants you to be. So in order to see how strong you are, Satan is going to try you, and he is always going to go to the Lord for permission.

Satan said, does Job fear God for nothing? Have you not made a hedge about him and blessed the work of his hands? Satan is telling the Most High that Job is only worshiping Him because He gives him a lot of stuff. That is the same thing with us today. When everything is going good you do not hear nothing from us; as soon as things go bad, that is when we start complaining and moaning and groaning. Satan said put forth thine hand and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face. The Lord said, behold, all that he hath is in thy power, only upon himself put not forth thine hand. In Christianity they teach that Satan and God had a fight and Satan rebelled and took a third of the angels. That does not sound like what is right here. Job was the subject of discussion between Satan and the Lord, and Satan needed permission from the Lord to mess with him. A lot of times in Christianity people think everything bad comes from the devil and everything good comes from God. Wrong. Both good and evil come from the Lord. Satan is not a free spirit out here doing his own thing; he is subject to God, much like us. -

Job lost his oxen: the Sabeans fell upon them, took them away, and slew the servants with the edge of the sword. That is problem number one. While the first messenger was yet speaking, another came: the fire of God fell from heaven and burned up the sheep and the servants. That is problem number two. While he was yet speaking, another came: the Chaldeans made out three bands, fell upon the camels, carried them away, and slew the servants. That is problem number three. While he was yet speaking, another came: a great wind from the wilderness smote the four corners of the house and it fell upon the young men and they are dead. Job just lost his cattle, his servants, and his children. Job just lost everything. Why? Because the devil, with the permission of the Lord, was able to put his hand on Job to try him. That is what we need as Israelites; when we do certain things the Lord gives us certain things, and He has to try them to see if the heart is still going to be the same way. -

Job rent his mantle, shaved his head, fell down and worshiped, and said naked came I out of my mother's womb and naked shall I return; the Lord gave and the Lord hath taken away, blessed be the name of the Lord. In all this Job sinned not nor charged God foolishly. Job understood it: everything that we have comes from the Lord, everything that we get comes from the Lord. What good is it for us to blame God for stuff that we lose, when He can give it right back to you? There is nothing in this world that you can get yourself without the help of the Lord, unless you serve Satan and he gives it to you, but do you really want to pay that price? Even then it was the Lord that gave it to you, because the Lord handed you over to Satan; He put that stumbling block before you and you fell over it. -

Again there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also. The Lord said, hast thou considered My servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, and still he holdeth fast his integrity, although thou movedst Me against him to destroy him without cause. The Lord is bragging, He is boasting: even though you made Me go after Job for no reason at all, he is still standing strong, he is still handling his business. We have to allow God to brag on us. It is the same thing with all our enemies watching online; you have got to give the Lord a chance to brag.

Satan said, skin for skin, all that a man hath will he give for his life, but put forth thine hand now and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will curse thee to thy face. Possessions are possessions; a brother could lose a car, a job, family members, whatever. But Satan is saying if his health is afflicted, I bet you he will curse you to your face, because that is another thing that gets us. A lot of us, material things are not your stronghold. Even if you lost it today it would not do you nothing, but your health, that is your trial. As soon as you get sick you think it is the end of the world, or you think you did something. Maybe the Lord is doing this to you so you can be a shining light to somebody going through the same thing. A lot of our trials are not just for us. We read the book of Job because Job went through the things that we go through ourselves. The Lord said, behold, he is in thine hand, but save his life. The Lord said touch him but do not kill him. That does not sound like somebody rebellious against God; Satan took orders, just like we take orders.
Satan went forth and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown, and Job took a potsherd to scrape himself withal, and he sat down among the ashes.

Then his wife said, dost thou still retain thine integrity? Curse God, and die. This is the other test that brothers get. Satan is going to come through your woman. If he cannot get to you, he is going to come through her. Look at what he did with Adam: Satan was not going to get past Adam, so he backdoored and went to Eve. Same thing here; Satan was in his woman too. A lot of men, we get emotional behind our woman, and whatever she wants to say we go follow it instead of checking her. Job said, thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh; what, shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips. So he told her, woman, you sound foolish. Are we only going to get good from God and not evil? That is what we tell people all the time. We just read in [Isaiah 45:7](/bible/isaiah/45#v7) that God creates evil and creates peace. God is a man of war; He creates life and death. Nothing happens without the Lord; everything asks for permission.

Job's three friends heard of all this evil that came upon him: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. They made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him. When they lifted up their eyes afar off and knew him not, they lifted up their voice and wept, rent every man his mantle, and sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven. They sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word, for they saw that his grief was very great. Much like us, our friends hear of our affliction and come to lend their support, to give correction, to give harsh reality and hard truth. We are not talking about people that butter you up knowing you are in the wrong; we are talking about people that give you straight facts about what is going on with you.

Job continues his parable and remembers the months past when the Most High preserved him, when His candle shined upon his head and by His light Job walked through darkness. These were the days of his youth, when the secret of God was upon his tabernacle, when the Almighty was yet with him and his children were about him, when he washed his steps with butter and the rock poured him out rivers of oil. Remember verse 1 says Job continued his parable. A lot of what Job is talking about, not the entire book but a lot of it, is in parable form, and most of it is above the pay grade.

When Job went out to the gate of the city and prepared his seat in the street, the young men saw him and hid themselves, and the aged arose and stood up. The princes refrained talking and laid their hand on their mouth. The nobles held their peace and their tongue cleaved to the roof of their mouth. When the ear heard him it blessed him, and when the eye saw him it gave witness to him.

Job delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him. The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon him, and he caused the widow's heart to sing for joy. He put on righteousness and it clothed him, his judgment was as a robe and a diadem. He was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame, a father to the poor, and he searched out the cause he knew not. He broke the jaws of the wicked and plucked the spoil out of his teeth.

Then Job said he would die in his nest and multiply his days as the sand. His root was spread out by the waters and the dew lay all night upon his branch. His glory was fresh in him and his bow was renewed in his hand.

Men gave ear to Job and waited and kept silence at his counsel. After his words they spake not again, and his speech dropped upon them. They waited for him as for the rain and opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain. If he laughed on them they believed it not, and the light of his countenance they cast not down. He chose out their way and sat chief, dwelling as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners. This is a deep parable by Job.

Job made a covenant with his eyes, so why then should he think upon a maid? He asks what portion of God is there from above and what inheritance of the Almighty from on high. Is not destruction to the wicked and a strange punishment to the workers of iniquity? This is the chapter where it is clear and obvious that Job is starting to justify himself, which is where he actually made his mistake. He asks that he be weighed in an even balance that God may know his integrity.

If his step turned out of the way, or his heart walked after his eyes, or any blot cleaved to his hands, then let him sow and let another eat, and let his offspring be rooted out. If his heart was deceived by a woman or he laid wait at his neighbor's door, then let his wife grind unto another and let others bow down upon her. Job is saying if he committed adultery let the same come back on him, for this is a heinous crime, a fire that consumeth to destruction and would root out all his increase. -

If Job despised the cause of his manservant or maidservant when they contended with him, what then would he do when God riseth up and visiteth? What would he answer? Did not He that made Job in the womb make his servant also, and did not one fashion them both in the womb?

If Job withheld the poor from their desire, caused the widow's eyes to fail, or ate his morsel alone while the fatherless did not eat, then let judgment come. From his youth the fatherless was brought up with him as with a father, and he guided the widow from his mother's womb. If he saw any perish for lack of clothing, or any poor without covering, whose loins did not bless him when warmed with the fleece of his sheep; if he lifted up his hand against the fatherless when he saw his help in the gate, then let his arm fall from his shoulder blade and be broken from the bone. He is justifying himself, saying I help people, I do this, I do that. For destruction from God was a terror to him and by reason of His highness he could not endure.

If Job made gold his hope or said to the fine gold, Thou art my confidence; if he rejoiced because his wealth was great and his hand had gotten much; then it would be iniquity. If he beheld the sun when it shined or the moon walking in brightness, and his heart was secretly enticed, or his mouth kissed his hand, this also were an iniquity to be punished by the judge, for he should have denied the God that is above.

Job did not rejoice at the destruction of him that hated him nor lift up himself when evil found him; neither did he suffer his mouth to sin by wishing a curse to his enemy's soul. The men of his tabernacle did not go unsatisfied; the stranger did not lodge in the street, for he opened his doors to the traveler. He did not cover his transgression as Adam by hiding his iniquity in his bosom, nor did he fear a great multitude or the contempt of families to the point of keeping silence.

Job desires that the Almighty would answer him, and that his adversary had written a book. Surely he would take it upon his shoulder and bind it as a crown, and declare unto Him the number of his steps as a prince. If his land cried against him or its furrows complained, if he ate its fruits without money or caused its owners to lose their life, then let thistles grow instead of wheat and cockle instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.

Job answers the Most High and confesses that He can do everything and that no thought can be withholden from Him. This is a little thing in the scriptures to take heed to: the Most High hears our words and our thoughts, so the hatred or the private spirit a man carries cannot be hidden from Him. He knows the inward parts of men. Job says he uttered what he understood not, things too wonderful for him which he knew not. He had heard of the Most High by the hearing of the ear, but now his eye sees Him, and therefore he abhors himself and repents in dust and ashes. Dust and ashes refer to the custom our forefathers had of putting ashes on the head as a sign of sorrow and repentance. -

After the Most High had spoken these words, He tells Eliphaz the Temanite that His wrath is kindled against him and his two friends, because they have not spoken of Him the thing that is right, as His servant Job has. Throughout the book Job's three friends dealt wrongly with him after his children were killed and everything was taken, so they did not deal righteously as their brother Job did. He commands them to take seven bullocks and seven rams and go to Job and offer a burnt offering for themselves, and Job will pray for them, for him will He accept, lest He deal with them after their folly. The sacrifice for their sin had to be brought to Job, the righteous one in the situation. This is how the priesthood worked, all the way from Leviticus and the five books throughout history: we brought the sacrifice to the Levites and priests and they did it on our behalf, and if a man did not bring his sacrifice, the Most High would deal with him and what he did would not be forgiven. Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the Most High commanded, and He accepted Job. -

The Most High turned the captivity of Job when he prayed for his friends, and gave him twice as much as he had before. It was not the prayer alone that availed, but the prayer of a righteous man, so the Most High deals with those that are dealing in righteousness. Then all his brethren, sisters, and former acquaintances came and ate bread with him, bemoaned him, and comforted him over all the evil the Most High had brought upon him, and every man gave him a piece of money and an earring of gold. After his captivity was turned his friends returned as well. -

The Most High blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses, along with seven sons and three daughters. He named the daughters Jemima, Kezia, and Keren-happuch, and in all the land were no women found so fair, and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren. Job lived a hundred and forty years after this and saw his sons and his sons' sons, even four generations, and died being old and full of days. He received much more than he had in the beginning, all because he stayed faithful to the Most High through the whole trial. The purpose of the trial was to see whether Job would fix himself and stay faithful or curse the Most High. The same thing happens to us: we endure to the end as Job did, and at some point the Most High will turn the captivity of the Israelites who kept the commandments and repay them for all their righteousness, far more than double the houses, families, cars, and jobs we have now, giving us much more in the kingdom. -

Certain of the elders of Israel came and sat before Ezekiel, and the word of the Lord said these men have set up their idols in their hearts, setting up something above God, and put the stumbling block of their iniquity before their face. The Most High asks whether He should be inquired of at all by them. Every man of the house of Israel that sets up his idols in his heart and comes to the prophet, the Lord will answer according to the multitude of his idols, that He may take the house of Israel in their own heart, because they are all estranged from Him through their idols and spiritual idolatry.

The Most High tells the house of Israel to repent, come back to His laws, and turn themselves from their idols and away from all their abominations. Every one of the house of Israel, or the stranger that sojourns in Israel, who separates himself from Him and sets up idols in his heart and comes to a prophet to inquire, the Lord will answer by Himself and set His face against that man. He will make him a sign and a proverb, meaning a curse, and cut him off from the midst of His people as an example, that they may know He is the Lord.

If a prophet is deceived when he has spoken a thing, the Lord Himself has deceived that prophet; do not try to deceive yourself in this truth, and when we get counsel we should take it and keep it moving. He will stretch out His hand upon that prophet and destroy him from the midst of His people Israel, and both shall bear the punishment of their iniquity. This is so the house of Israel may go no more astray from Him nor be polluted any more with their transgressions, but be His people and He their God. -

The word of the Lord came saying that when a land sins by trespassing grievously, He will stretch out His hand upon it, break the staff of its bread, and send famine to cut off man and beast. Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness. No one can save anyone else; it does not matter who you are or what your status is in Israel, you have to save yourself by your own righteousness.

If He causes noisome beasts to pass through the land and spoil it so that it is desolate and no man may pass through, this is one of His judgments. Though these three men were in it, as the Lord lives they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters; they only shall be delivered by their righteousness, but the land shall be desolate.

If He brings a sword upon that land to cut off man and beast, though these three men were in it, they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters. They only shall deliver themselves by their righteousness.

If He sends a pestilence into the land and pours out His fury upon it in blood to cut off man and beast, though Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, they shall deliver neither son nor daughter. They shall but deliver their own souls by their righteousness; everyone has to work out their own righteousness in fear and trembling, delivering their own soul by keeping the Most High's commandments. -

How much more when the Most High sends His four sore judgments upon Jerusalem, the sword, the famine, the noisome beast, and the pestilence, to cut off man and beast; and these are not just for back then but for today. Behold, a remnant shall be left, both sons and daughters, that shall be brought forth unto you, and you shall see their ways and their doings. You shall be comforted concerning the evil the Most High brought upon Jerusalem when you see their ways, and you shall know He has not done without cause all that He has done in it. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry)

verses.text: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and eschewed evil.
And there were born unto him seven sons and three daughters.

His substance also was seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she asses, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the men of the east.
And his sons went and feasted in their houses, every one his day; and sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.

And it was so, when the days of their feasting were gone about, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all: for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.
And the Lord said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil?
Then Job arose, and rent his mantle, and shaved his head, and fell down upon the ground, and worshipped,
And said, Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.
In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.

And the Lord said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil? and still he holdeth fast his integrity, although thou movedst me against him, to destroy him without cause.
When the ear heard me, then it blessed me; and when the eye saw me, it gave witness to me:
Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him.
The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me: and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.
I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: my judgment was as a robe and a diadem.
I was eyes to the blind, and feet was I to the lame.
I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out.
And I brake the jaws of the wicked, and plucked the spoil out of his teeth.
I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?
And the Lord turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before.

Then came there unto him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, and did eat bread with him in his house: and they bemoaned him, and comforted him over all the evil that the Lord had brought upon him: every man also gave him a piece of money, and every one an earring of gold.
So the Lord blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.
He had also seven sons and three daughters.
And he called the name of the first, Jemima; and the name of the second, Kezia; and the name of the third, Keren–happuch.
And in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.
After this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons’ sons, even four generations.
So Job died, being old and full of days.
Behold, we count them happy which endure. Ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord; that the Lord is very pitiful, and of tender mercy.
Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness, saith the Lord God.

And the Lord turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before.

Then came there unto him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, and did eat bread with him in his house: and they bemoaned him, and comforted him over all the evil that the Lord had brought upon him: every man also gave him a piece of money, and every one an earring of gold.
So the Lord blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.
He had also seven sons and three daughters.
And he called the name of the first, Jemima; and the name of the second, Kezia; and the name of the third, Keren–happuch.
And in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.
After this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons’ sons, even four generations.
So Job died, being old and full of days.
Behold, we count them happy which endure. Ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord; that the Lord is very pitiful, and of tender mercy.
Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness, saith the Lord God.
